Co-author of ESM3, a language model for protein design; at Anthropic researches how Claude internally represents emotional concepts; previously Director at the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff, Applied AI (Agentic Coding)
contribucion_destacada: Works on Claude's agentic coding capabilities on the Applied AI team; publishes technical research on harness design and generator-evaluator architectures.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (former CEO and co-founder of Humanloop)
contribucion_destacada: Co-founder and CEO of Humanloop (evals platform for enterprise LLMs); joined Anthropic in August 2025 with the entire founding team.
Product Manager/Designer at Anthropic since January 2026; previously built the mobile and desktop teams at Figma; launched Claude Design and mobile features of Claude.
Inference researcher at Anthropic; developed Constitutional Classifiers++, efficient safeguards against universal jailbreaks.
Author of R-CNN and Fast R-CNN, co-creator of YOLO and lead of Segment Anything/SAM 2; previously at FAIR (Meta), Allen Institute for AI and Microsoft Research.
Co-founder of xAI (the last of the 11 founders to leave the company); joined Anthropic to focus on compute after the SpaceX compute deal (Colossus 1).

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff, Interpretability & Alignment
contribucion_destacada: Researcher with more than 2,900 citations in mechanistic interpretability; developed Circuit Breakers and the Petri auditing tool; on leave from Harvard.
Co-author, using Claude, of the construction of Hadamard matrices of twelve previously unknown orders (August 2026).
Co-author of Anthropic's early research on RLHF ('Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant') and on moral self-correction in LLMs.
Co-author of the RLHF and Claude technical reports; researches sycophancy in models; co-founder of Hofvarpnir Studios.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff, Discovery (Claude for scientific computing)
contribucion_destacada: Assistant professor of Computing, Data Science and Physics at Boston University; at Anthropic researches how AI can accelerate the scientific process (long-running agentic scientific computing).
Representation learning and computer vision researcher with more than 66,000 citations; previously Staff/Senior Research Scientist at Google DeepMind and Google Brain.
RL, game theory and LLM researcher at Anthropic; developed the DeepNash algorithm for expert-level Stratego.

Co-author of 'Language Models Can Explain Neurons in Language Models' (with Jan Leike, Ilya Sutskever and others) at OpenAI; now in interpretability at Anthropic; also previously a Senior Staff Software Engineer at Google.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (former CEO of Kandra Labs, Zulip lead)
contribucion_destacada: Lead developer of the open-source Zulip project and CEO of Kandra Labs; previously founder and CTO of Ksplice; joined Anthropic in May 2026 together with three other veteran Zulip leaders.
AI agents and MCP researcher at Anthropic; lead author of the International AI Safety Report 2025; previously Head of AI Agents at WorkOS.
Formerly on the Preparedness, Safety Systems and Multiagent teams at OpenAI; joined an amicus brief by former OpenAI employees questioning the integrity of its leadership; now at Anthropic.
Co-author of OpenAI's scaling laws and of Constitutional AI; at Anthropic works on interpretability (Scaling Monosemanticity).
Was one of the leaders of the Borg team (Google's cluster management system) and a maintainer of Kubernetes and Docker's libcontainer; now in infrastructure at Anthropic.
Mechanistic interpretability researcher at Anthropic; known for his work on how LLMs represent space and time, and for identifying a vector that controls models' refusal behavior.
Co-author of RT-2 (vision-language-action model for robotics); now develops alignment algorithms for LLMs (factuality and resistance to manipulation).
First author of WARM (weight averaged reward models) and Rewarded Soups; co-author of Gemini 2.5; 2024 SSFAM award for the best French ML thesis.
Co-author of Min-p sampling and lead author of BatchBALD and RHO-loss; PhD with Yarin Gal (Oxford); previously at Midjourney.
Led the launch of Gemma Scope 2 and SAEBench; co-creator of the ARENA program; co-author of Scaling Monosemanticity during his time at Anthropic.
Co-author of DiscoRL (Nature) and Gemini 2.5; creator of Datarater (data curation with meta-learned reward models); at DeepMind since 2019.
Co-author of MONA (reducing multi-turn reward hacking) and of scheming and stealth evaluations; MATS mentor.
Co-author of 'Chain of Thought Monitorability' and 'Foundational Challenges in Assuring Alignment and Safety of LLMs'; creator of STARC (distance between reward functions).
Co-author with Will MacAskill of 'Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion'; Post-AGI researcher at Google DeepMind; previously Forethought and the Future of Humanity Institute.
Co-author of the Differentiable Neural Computer (Nature, 2016) and of work on memory in RL; MIT Technology Review Innovators Under 35.
Co-author of Deterministic Policy Gradient and Value-Decomposition Networks (multi-agent RL); contributor to Gemini Robotics 1.5.
Led the Inverse Scaling Prize (2023), a collaborative study of cases where larger models perform worse.

cargo_literal: Visiting Researcher, Google DeepMind (University of Washington professor of Mathematics, on leave)
contribucion_destacada: Walker Family Professor of Mathematics (UW) on leave at Google DeepMind for AI applied to mathematics; invited speaker at ICM 2026.
First author of 'General agents contain world models' (ICML 2025) and 'Robust agents learn causal world models'.
Researches evaluation of LLM moral competence and morally significant AI at Google DeepMind; covered in MIT Technology Review; previously assistant professor of Philosophy.
First author of 'Masked Language Model Scoring'; develops streaming audio generation models (duplex voice and music) for Gemini Live and Project Astra; co-author of Gemini 2.5.
Co-author of Gemma Scope, JumpReLU SAEs and Tracr; co-creator of OpenSpiel (RL framework for games).
Research on memory, the hippocampus and predictive representations in RL; MIT Technology Review Innovators Under 35 (2019); adjunct professor at Columbia.
First author of 'Ethical and social risks of harm from language models' and of DeepMind's sociotechnical safety evaluation framework; co-author of Gemini and Gopher.

cargo_literal: Senior Research Scientist (AGI Safety and Alignment)
contribucion_destacada: Lead co-author of 'Evaluating Frontier Models for Dangerous Capabilities'; works on loss-of-control risk preparedness at Google DeepMind.
Co-creator of Tracr (compiler from programs to transformers); contributor to Gemini, Gemma 2 and Imagen 3; work on specification gaming and dangerous-capability evaluation.
Co-author of the 'Habermas Machine' (AI for democratic deliberation, Science) and of value profiles; works on LLM safety and alignment.
Founder of the Quantified Uncertainty Research Institute; creator of Guesstimate and Squiggle; previously at the Future of Humanity Institute.
Foundational RL research (representations, network sparsity, scalability); co-creator of Dopamine (RL framework) and 'Rigging the Lottery'.
Co-creator of Tacotron 2 and co-lead of BIG-bench; work on audio generation, probabilistic ML and TensorFlow Distributions.
Creator of rr (record-and-replay debugger) and co-founder of Pernosco; Mozilla distinguished engineer; now at Google DeepMind.
Led Decoupled DiLoCo (fault-tolerant distributed pretraining across millions of TPUs); contributor to the JAX/XLA/TPU stack.

First author of 'Data Distributional Properties Drive Emergent In-Context Learning in Transformers' and co-author of Many-Shot In-Context Learning and Genie; building a team on the societal impacts of AI.
Director of the CAP Lab at NYU (computational psycholinguistics and neural network evaluation); researcher at Google Research since 2021.
Co-author of AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, MuZero, AlphaCode, AlphaTensor, AlphaDev and AlphaProof.
Creator of the AI Safety Gridworlds; leads the Causal Incentives Working Group; ICLR 2025 keynote on AGI safety and causality.
First author of Gemma Scope and co-author of JumpReLU SAEs, Gated SAEs and ATP*.
Author of LintSeq and co-author of BALROG, ARE and Gaia2 (agent evaluation and training); PhD at NYU Courant.

cargo_literal: Senior Research Scientist (AGI Safety and Alignment)
contribucion_destacada: Creator of the AI Safety Gridworlds and author of work on specification gaming and deceptive alignment; co-founder of the Future of Life Institute.

cargo_literal: Senior Staff Research Engineer; tech lead for sparse autoencoders
contribucion_destacada: Tech lead of the sparse autoencoders effort at Google DeepMind (Gated SAEs); first author of 'Explaining grokking through circuit efficiency' and 'Challenges with unsupervised LLM knowledge discovery'.
Author of 'Catastrophic Jailbreak' and co-creator of SORRY-Bench; co-author of Gemini 2.5 and contributor to Gemini's gold at IMO 2025.
First author of ToolQA and AdaPlanner; works on reasoning and post-training for Gemini 3.0 and 3.1.

cargo_literal: Research Engineer; Tech Lead, Frontier Safety Mitigations (AGI Safety and Alignment)
contribucion_destacada: Tech lead for Frontier Safety mitigations at Google DeepMind (safeguards against cyber and biological risks); writes publicly about his AI safety work.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff, Infra & Performance
contribucion_destacada: First author of Striped Attention and FlashFormer (whole-model kernels for low-batch inference); co-author of Cross-Layer Attention (KV cache reduction).
Co-creator of Multi-News, FOLIO and QAFactEval (summarization and factual consistency of LLMs); PhD at Yale.
First author of AWAC and RIG and co-author of Implicit Q-Learning (offline and self-supervised RL for robotics); co-author of the GPT-4 report; PhD at BAIR (Berkeley).
Co-author of JailbreakBench, AgentDojo and CaMeL ('Defeating prompt injections by design') and of RobustBench; PhD student at ETH Zürich.
First author of 'Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection' (ICLR 2025); works on model psychology and character; MATS mentor.

cargo_literal: Research Scientist (Meta TBD Lab, inteligencia multimodal)
contribucion_destacada: Lead author of MaskGIT and Muse, and co-author of Imagic, Palette and MAGVIT (image and video generation); co-author of the GPT-4o system card; joined Meta in July 2025.
Researcher in ML systems security and AI agents (model collapse, extraction attacks and prompt injection); previously Senior Research Scientist at Google DeepMind.
Formerly head of Scale AI's Safety, Evaluations, and Alignment Lab (SEAL); at Meta works on AI alignment with Summer Yue and Alexandr Wang.
First author of 'Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think' (chain-of-thought faithfulness); safety and alignment evaluations for Meta's superintelligence initiative.

Safety, robustness and alignment researcher at Meta Superintelligence Labs; co-author of 'Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models'; previously Scale AI and the Center for AI Safety.
Former CEO of Ai2 (July 2023 – March 2026).
licencia_foto: CC BY 2.0

cargo_literal: Principal Applied Scientist and Manager (Microsoft AI)
contribucion_destacada: First author of 'Underspecification Presents Challenges for Credibility in Modern ML' and Healthsheet; co-author of Gemini; previously Google DeepMind and head of AI at Robin AI.
Co-inventor of AdaBoost and pioneer of boosting (Gödel Prize 2003); member of the NAS and the NAE; researcher at Microsoft Research since 2014; previously professor at Princeton.
Lead co-author of Go-Explore ('First return, then explore') and co-author of the GPT-4 report and Weak-to-strong generalization; works on LLM scaling.
Creator of AidanBench (LLM creativity); contributed to the GPT-4.5 and GPT-5 system cards; active public presence on model design.
Presented OpenAI's experimental reasoning model with gold-medal performance at IMO 2025; co-author of the o1 system card.

cargo_literal: Physicist, OpenAI for Science (first hire); Vanderbilt professor

contribucion_destacada: Offensive security researcher with public talks (OffensiveCon) on Secure Boot; now in Preparedness focused on agentic security.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (part-time; Harvard professor)
contribucion_destacada: Safety and alignment research at OpenAI (deliberative alignment, o1 system card); professor of Computer Science at Harvard.
Lead author of Unit Scaling and u-μP (parametrization for stable, low-precision training) and of SparQ Attention.
Worked on WebGPT, ChatGPT and GPT-4; contributed to the GPT-4o and GPT-5 system cards; appears on the OpenAI Podcast.
Co-founder of Software Applications (Sky, acquired by OpenAI in October 2025) and of Workflow, the origin of Apple Shortcuts.
Lead drafter of version 2 of OpenAI's Preparedness Framework; author of 'Voices in the Code'; co-founder of Upturn.
Researches RL algorithms for general-purpose agents; first author of work on in-context learning and compositional generalization (PhD at MIT).
Built OpenAI's early research supercomputing infrastructure and was part of the initial ChatGPT team; speaker at Datadog DASH 2019; co-author of GPT-3.
Lead author of 'Let's Verify Step by Step' (process supervision with reward models); contributed to the o1 and GPT-5 system cards.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff, Developer Experience
contribucion_destacada: Led the technical development of Swarm (precursor to the Agents SDK) and contributed to Codex CLI; public talks on fine-tuning and agents.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (Research Scientist), Pretraining
contribucion_destacada: Lead co-author of 'Emergent Tool Use from Multi-Agent Autocurricula' (hide-and-seek); co-author of the GPT-4 report; at OpenAI since 2018.
Works on alignment at OpenAI; drove the OpenAI Safety Fellowship; previously at the UK AI Security Institute.
Lead Scientist at EleutherAI: co-author of The Pile, GPT-NeoX-20B and BLOOM; co-author of the GPT-4o system card.
Helped write and maintains OpenAI's Model Spec, the public framework for the intended behavior of models.
Author of DiffusionDB, CNN Explainer, WizMap and Farsight (interactive interfaces for interpreting ML); Forbes 30 Under 30 in Science; PhD at Georgia Tech.
Co-creator of Llama Guard and lead safety contributor to Llama 3; previously Staff Research Scientist at Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Key GPT-4.5 researcher at OpenAI; her 2025 green card denial case had wide press coverage.
Co-lead of GPT-4 safety evaluations at OpenAI; PhD at MIT on robust and reliable ML.
Creator of the Muon optimizer (December 2024 blog post) and of training speed records on NanoGPT and CIFAR-10.
Creator of The Pile and co-author of the LM Evaluation Harness (EleutherAI); co-author of the GPT-4 technical report.
First author of InstructGPT ('Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback'), the pioneering application of RLHF to LLMs; co-author of WebGPT, GPT-4 and GPT-4o.
Previously led Gemini post-training for memory, tool use and audio at Google DeepMind; co-author of Gemini 2.5; now works on agent reliability at OpenAI.
Works on misalignment/scheming monitoring at OpenAI (reviews 99.9% of internal coding traffic); co-author of 'Targeted Manipulation and Deception'.
First author of 'Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models' (alignment of the o-series models).
Lead author of Trajectory Transformer, Planning with Diffusion (Diffuser) and MBPO in RL; GPT-4o contributor.
Co-author of Codex, GPT-4 and 'Training Verifiers'; leads RL infrastructure and scaling work at OpenAI; previously technical advisor to the CEO.
Presented OpenAI's reasoning system with a perfect 12/12 score at the ICPC World Finals 2025; o1 contributor.
One of the leaders of the GPT-4o mini project and a contributor to GPT-4o; works on large-scale pretraining.
Built OpenAI's current LLM training stack and took part in training GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; co-author of the GPT-4 technical report.
Author of PAIR (automatic semantic jailbreaks) and co-creator of JailbreakBench; contributor to the GPT-4o and o1 system cards.
Core maintainer of the Triton compiler (OpenAI Triton) and co-author of 'Linear Layouts'; previously in compilers at Intel and Apple.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (Research Scientist), Pretraining
contribucion_destacada: Lead co-author of MoEUT (Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformer) and of work on compositional generalization; researches architectures for future LLMs.
Creator of StrongREJECT and Tensor Trust; co-author of Deliberative Alignment and the o1 system card.
Public AI agent security research (ShadowLeak, link safety); discoverer of CVE-2022-41034 in VSCode; speaker at Stanford.
Works on LLM agent monitoring and chain-of-thought monitorability; co-author of 'The Reversal Curse' and 'Towards understanding sycophancy'; MATS mentor.

cargo_literal: Post-training Multimodal Infrastructure leads (GPT-4o, 2024); also gpt-oss (2025)

contribucion_destacada: First author of 'Fine-tuning aligned language models compromises safety' and 'Safety alignment should be made more than just a few tokens deep'; creator of SORRY-Bench.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (generative models and multimodal understanding)
contribucion_destacada: Co-founder of Reve (controllable image generation research, acquired by OpenAI); vision model interpretability researcher and assistant professor at TTIC (on leave).
First author of DoLa, Lookback Lens and SelfCite (factuality and hallucinations in LLMs); joined OpenAI in 2023 to work on o1.
Creator of Llemma (open LLM for mathematics), ProofNet and OpenWebMath; previously worked on reasoning at xAI (Grok 3 and 4).
Co-author of INTELLECT-1, SmolLM2, SmolLM3 and The Common Pile; work on pretraining and open science.
Spent a year on FDM-1, a foundation model that learns from computer-use video; pretraining research on computer use.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff, ML Infra (founding engineer)
contribucion_destacada: Founding engineer at Thinking Machines Lab; previously worked on PyTorch Core Compilers; co-author of 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference'; author of the blog 'Thonk From First Principles'.
Co-author of "The Intelligence Curse" and co-founder of Workshop Labs, which joined Thinking Machines Lab in April 2026; previously AI governance lead at BlueDot Impact.

cargo_literal: Member of Technical Staff (forecasting and strategy)
contribucion_destacada: Co-author of 'The Intelligence Curse' and co-founder of Workshop Labs (user-aligned models), which joined Thinking Machines Lab; previously AI governance lead at BlueDot Impact.
Lead author of ProRL (extending the frontiers of reasoning with RL) and LMFlow (NAACL award-winning toolkit); co-author of Hymba and R-Tuning; previously at NVIDIA.
